epics.title: ATS Phase 1 MVP Discovery

items.title: Author the ATS discovery Skill definition and interview flow
items.description: Write the standalone ATS discovery Skill so it plugs into the existing guided-interview flow. It opens with leadership's vision, asks one question per reply, covers each stage of the staffing lifecycle, uses research only to test decisions, and narrows Phase 1 to the smallest usable end-to-end workflow. Unanswered topics are recorded as unresolved, not skipped silently.
definitionOfDone: Skill document exists, follows the repository's Skill format, and is selectable as an interview Skill option
Skill opens with leadership's vision before any market research
Skill lists every staffing lifecycle area and requires each to be covered or labeled unresolved
Skill states the rule that Phase 1 is the smallest usable end-to-end workflow and everything else is deferred
A scripted session confirms the Skill asks one question per reply
technicalDependencies: Existing guided-interview flow loads the Skill selected in project skill settings
ATS ADR (research-grounded-ats-discovery-skill) supplies the lifecycle areas and scope decisions
nonFunctionalRequirements: Skill must work with the existing interview streaming and thread persistence without runtime changes
Each reply asks exactly one question

items.title: Define decision ledger rules and conflict handling
items.description: Add the ledger section to the Skill. It defines the four decision states, requires each reply to show the current ledger, requires the interview to pause on a conflict until the leader names the authoritative decision, and requires the final ledger to be written into the standard interview transcript. The ledger uses reply text and existing persistence only.
definitionOfDone: Skill defines confirmed, assumed, unresolved, and superseded with one example each
Skill requires a visible ledger update in each reply that changes a decision
Skill requires a pause and a question when two decisions conflict
Skill requires the final ledger in the transcript used for PRD generation
Scripted sessions cover confirm, assume, skip, supersede, and conflict cases
technicalDependencies: Existing chat thread and interview transcript persistence hold the ledger text
TBI-001 interview flow defines where a ledger update appears in a reply
nonFunctionalRequirements: Ledger must survive thread resume with no loss of state
Ledger must stay short enough to show in every reply

items.title: Define research, source, and redaction rules
items.description: Add the research section to the Skill. It sets when research is allowed, lists the identifier types to redact before any query, defines acceptable sources, requires source and date on every recorded claim, requires citations on claims that influence scope, and requires corroboration for material claims. It includes a short benchmark seed list for the product owner to review during the pilot.
definitionOfDone: Skill lists the identifier types to redact and the step that redacts them before each query
Skill defines source rules and requires source and date for every recorded claim
Skill defines material claim and corroboration in the terms of the PRD
Skill includes a benchmark seed list marked for review during the pilot
Seeded test inputs with identifiers produce research queries with no leaked identifiers
technicalDependencies: Project-configured web research access is enabled for the pilot project
TBI-001 interview flow defines when a decision is ready to test
nonFunctionalRequirements: Research queries must contain no personal, client, commercial, or internal identifiers
Research must not leave a reply without visible status

items.title: Define completion rubric and PRD-ready output contract
items.description: Add the completion section to the Skill. It states when a session may finish, requires a Phase 1 brief, deferred roadmap, and research notes in the interview transcript in a form PRD generation reads, and keeps incomplete sessions as drafts.
definitionOfDone: Skill states the completion checks: coverage or unresolved labels, no open conflict, citations and corroboration present
Skill defines the structure of the Phase 1 brief, deferred roadmap, and research notes
Skill states that an incomplete session remains a draft
A finished test transcript is accepted by PRD generation and yields a usable PRD
technicalDependencies: PRD generation reads the finished interview transcript
Decision ledger and research rules from TBI-002 and TBI-003
nonFunctionalRequirements: Output must be readable by PRD generation without manual rewriting
Deferred scope must be kept apart from Phase 1 scope

items.title: Configure the pilot project and fallback
items.description: Write the pilot runbook and the configuration values for one project: register the ATS discovery Skill as an interview Skill option in project skill settings, enable web research and set the model, and confirm the existing interview Skill still starts. Describe how to remove the option.
definitionOfDone: Runbook names the settings to change and the values to use for the pilot project
ATS discovery Skill appears as an interview option only in the pilot project
Existing interview Skill still starts in the pilot project
Runbook describes how a Project Admin removes the option
technicalDependencies: Existing project skill settings support interview Skill options, web research, and model selection per project
Completed Skill from TBI-001 through TBI-004
nonFunctionalRequirements: Configuration must affect only the pilot project
Removing the option must leave in-progress threads readable

items.title: Define pilot scenarios and acceptance checklist
items.description: Write the pilot scenarios and a checklist that maps each pass condition to an observable check: lifecycle coverage, decision retention, citations, corroboration, resume, permissions, and Product-Owner acceptance. Record where results are kept and what counts as a runtime gap.
definitionOfDone: Checklist has one observable check per pass condition
Scenarios cover a normal run, a conflict, a resume after a break, and a run with seeded identifiers
Checklist includes a permission check for view-only users
Document states which findings count as a runtime gap needing a separate PRD
technicalDependencies: Existing interview resume and permission behavior
nonFunctionalRequirements: Checklist must use pass or fail checks with no numeric score
Scenarios must run without production client data

items.title: Shape a Phase 1 MVP through a guided leadership interview

userStory.iWant: describe leadership's vision and be guided through the staffing lifecycle to a Phase 1 MVP
userStory.soThat: leadership agrees on the smallest usable end-to-end workflow for the replacement ATS

outOfScope: Feature-parity checklist against eRecruit or the market
Changes to the interview UI
businessRules: BR-006: Cover the full lifecycle, narrow Phase 1 to the smallest usable workflow
BR-008: Existing project scope and interview permissions apply

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill opens by asking for leadership's vision, asks one question per reply, and works through every staffing lifecycle area before proposing Phase 1
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager starts an ATS discovery Interview
acceptanceCriteria.given: A Manager with interview manage permission has the ATS discovery Skill enabled in the project

acceptanceCriteria.then: The user sees an error in the chat, the thread keeps all earlier messages, and the user can resend or continue
acceptanceCriteria.when: A reply cannot be generated because the model or research step fails
acceptanceCriteria.given: An ATS discovery Interview is in progress

acceptanceCriteria.then: The area is recorded as unresolved and the interview moves on without asking again
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager chooses to skip it
acceptanceCriteria.given: Leadership cannot answer a lifecycle area

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill tests it against the smallest usable end-to-end workflow, and items outside that workflow go to the deferred roadmap rather than a parity checklist
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager submits that request
acceptanceCriteria.given: Leadership asks to include every feature of the old system or the market in Phase 1

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Only users who pass the existing interview permission checks for the project can start or continue the interview
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Replies stream through the existing interview chat with no added delay beyond research steps, which show a visible status
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The interview uses the existing chat view, so keyboard and screen reader behavior stay as they are

items.title: Keep a visible ledger of decisions

userStory.iWant: see which decisions are confirmed, assumed, unresolved, or superseded
userStory.soThat: leadership knows what is settled and what still needs an answer

outOfScope: A separate ledger table or screen
Export of the ledger to another system
businessRules: BR-002: Pause on conflict until the authoritative decision is named

acceptanceCriteria.then: The reply shows the decision with its state, and earlier decisions keep their states
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill replies
acceptanceCriteria.given: A decision has just been made in the interview

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Manager can correct it in chat and the Skill restores the correct state in the next reply
acceptanceCriteria.when: The model drops or misstates an earlier decision
acceptanceCriteria.given: The ledger is being rebuilt from a long conversation

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill quotes both without judgment, pauses, asks which is authoritative, and marks the other superseded
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager gives a new answer that conflicts with an earlier one
acceptanceCriteria.given: Two decisions are recorded for the same topic

acceptanceCriteria.then: The superseded decision stays visible as superseded and is never counted as confirmed
acceptanceCriteria.when: The ledger is shown again
acceptanceCriteria.given: A decision was marked superseded

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: The ledger is stored only in the existing project-scoped thread and transcript
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: The ledger is part of the reply text and adds no separate request
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The ledger is plain text in the chat so assistive technology reads it like any other message

items.title: Test Phase 1 decisions with cited research

userStory.iWant: see the cited sources behind claims that change Phase 1 scope
userStory.soThat: I can trust the scope decisions and check them

outOfScope: Research on topics unrelated to a Phase 1 decision
Automatic scoring of vendors
businessRules: BR-004: Research only when it informs a decision
BR-005: Citations on influential claims, corroboration on material claims

acceptanceCriteria.then: Each claim that influences scope shows a source and date, and each material claim shows a second independent source
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill researches it
acceptanceCriteria.given: A decision about Phase 1 scope is ready to test and research is enabled for the project

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill says so, labels the decision as assumed or unresolved, and does not state an uncited claim as fact
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill tries to test a decision
acceptanceCriteria.given: Web research is unavailable or returns nothing useful

acceptanceCriteria.then: The claim is marked uncorroborated and cannot support a confirmed decision until a second independent source is found
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill prepares to rely on it
acceptanceCriteria.given: A material claim has only one source

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill makes no research call and does not add a parity item from the market
acceptanceCriteria.when: The interview reaches that topic
acceptanceCriteria.given: A topic has no bearing on any open decision

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Research uses the project-configured web research access and only redacted queries
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Research runs only when a decision needs it, and the reply shows a status while it runs
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Citations appear as plain text with source name and date so assistive technology reads them

items.title: Keep sensitive ATS details out of web research

userStory.iWant: share real ATS context in the interview without it reaching public web searches
userStory.soThat: leadership can be candid without exposing people, clients, or commercial terms

outOfScope: Automated scanning tools outside the Skill instructions
Redaction of the stored interview conversation
businessRules: BR-003: Redact before any research query

acceptanceCriteria.then: The query uses generic descriptions in place of every one of those identifiers
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill runs a research query about a related decision
acceptanceCriteria.given: The Manager has named a client, a contract price, a person, and an internal system in the interview

acceptanceCriteria.then: It treats the term as an identifier, generalizes it, or asks the Manager before searching
acceptanceCriteria.when: It prepares a research query containing that term
acceptanceCriteria.given: The Skill cannot tell whether a term is an identifier

acceptanceCriteria.then: Only the generalized idea is searched and no part of the passage is copied
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill builds a query from that passage
acceptanceCriteria.given: An identifier appears inside a longer quoted passage

acceptanceCriteria.then: It declines to search with the name, explains why, and offers a generic search instead
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Skill receives the request
acceptanceCriteria.given: The Manager asks the Skill to search for a named client or person directly

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: No personal, client, commercial, or internal identifier appears in a research query, and research notes keep only sources and dates
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Redaction happens inside the reply that triggers research and adds no separate step for the user
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Any notice about redaction is shown as plain chat text

items.title: Pause and resume an ATS interview without losing decisions

userStory.iWant: pause an ATS discovery interview and resume it later
userStory.soThat: leaders can decide over several sittings without repeating earlier answers

outOfScope: Resume across projects
Merging two interviews
businessRules: BR-008: Existing interview resume and permissions apply

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill shows the ledger with every decision in its earlier state and asks the next open question
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager returns later and resumes the interview
acceptanceCriteria.given: An ATS discovery Interview is in progress with several decisions recorded

acceptanceCriteria.then: The user sees an error with a way to retry, and no earlier decisions are lost from storage
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager opens the interview
acceptanceCriteria.given: The thread cannot be loaded on resume

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill labels the affected decision as assumed or unresolved until it can be tested again
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager resumes
acceptanceCriteria.given: The interview ended mid-research on the previous sitting

acceptanceCriteria.then: The message is refused and the interview content stays unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.when: The user tries to send a message
acceptanceCriteria.given: A user with interview view permission only opens the interview

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Only users with access to the project and the interview can resume it
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Resuming opens the existing thread and continues in the next reply with no reload of earlier questions
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Resume uses the existing interview list and chat view

items.title: Receive a PRD-ready Phase 1 brief, deferred roadmap, and research notes

userStory.iWant: receive a Phase 1 brief, a deferred roadmap, and research notes when the interview ends
userStory.soThat: I can generate a PRD without rewriting the interview

outOfScope: Automatic PRD approval
Export of the outputs outside Apex
businessRules: BR-006: Phase 1 is the smallest usable workflow, the rest is deferred

acceptanceCriteria.then: The transcript holds a Phase 1 brief, a deferred roadmap, and research notes, and PRD generation can read it
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager confirms the final brief and the interview is completed
acceptanceCriteria.given: Every lifecycle area is covered or labeled unresolved and no conflict is open

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill names the gap and the session stays a draft until it is covered or labeled unresolved
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager asks to finish
acceptanceCriteria.given: A lifecycle area is neither covered nor labeled unresolved

acceptanceCriteria.then: The unresolved items are listed in the brief and the deferred roadmap, not stated as decided
acceptanceCriteria.when: The interview completes
acceptanceCriteria.given: Leadership stops with several decisions unresolved but all areas labeled

acceptanceCriteria.then: The Skill refuses to produce a completed brief and asks which decision is authoritative
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Manager asks to finish
acceptanceCriteria.given: An open conflict exists between two decisions

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: The outputs contain sources and dates, not redacted identifiers, and follow existing project scope
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: The outputs are produced in the closing reply of the interview with no separate job
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The outputs are structured text in the transcript, readable in the existing interview and PRD views

items.title: Enable the ATS discovery Skill for the pilot project

userStory.iWant: turn on the ATS discovery Skill for the pilot project in project skill settings
userStory.soThat: the pilot runs in one project while the existing interview Skill stays available

outOfScope: A new settings screen
Enabling the Skill in all projects at once
businessRules: BR-009: Fallback stays available and release is through project skill configuration
BR-008: No new permission, API, table, or UI

acceptanceCriteria.then: A Manager in that project can choose it when starting an interview, and the existing interview Skill is still listed
acceptanceCriteria.when: The admin adds the ATS discovery Skill as an interview option and enables web research
acceptanceCriteria.given: A Project Admin is in project skill settings for the pilot project

acceptanceCriteria.then: The user sees a clear error and can start the existing interview Skill instead
acceptanceCriteria.when: A Manager starts an interview with that option
acceptanceCriteria.given: The admin enters a Skill path that does not exist in the configured repository

acceptanceCriteria.then: The in-progress threads remain readable and new interviews no longer offer the option
acceptanceCriteria.when: The admin removes the option
acceptanceCriteria.given: Interviews are already in progress with the ATS discovery Skill

acceptanceCriteria.then: The change is refused and the settings stay unchanged
acceptanceCriteria.when: The user tries to add the ATS discovery Skill
acceptanceCriteria.given: A user without Project Admin rights opens project skill settings

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Only a Project Admin can change project skill settings, and the change applies to one project
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Saving the setting takes effect for new interviews without a deployment
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The change uses the existing project settings screen

items.title: Accept or reject the ATS discovery pilot

userStory.iWant: check the pilot against the agreed pass conditions and accept or reject it
userStory.soThat: wider use of the Skill rests on evidence and not on opinion alone

outOfScope: A quantitative score threshold
Automated pilot scoring
businessRules: BR-010: All pass conditions must hold and no numeric score is used

acceptanceCriteria.then: The pilot is recorded as passed and wider use may be planned
acceptanceCriteria.when: All six pass conditions are met and the Product-Owner accepts the PRD-ready output
acceptanceCriteria.given: A pilot interview has finished and the checklist is filled in

acceptanceCriteria.then: The pilot is recorded as not passed, the failure is named, and the Skill is revised before another pilot run
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Product-Owner reviews the checklist
acceptanceCriteria.given: A pass condition fails, such as a missing citation or a failed resume

acceptanceCriteria.then: It is logged as a runtime gap for a separate PRD and is not added to this scope
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Product-Owner records the finding
acceptanceCriteria.given: The pilot shows a requirement the existing runtime cannot meet

acceptanceCriteria.then: The pilot is not passed, because acceptance cannot be replaced by a score or by the other conditions
acceptanceCriteria.when: The Product-Owner records the result
acceptanceCriteria.given: Five conditions pass but the Product-Owner does not accept the output

nonFunctionalRequirements.security: Pilot records contain no redacted identifiers and stay within the project
nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Not applicable: the pilot review is a manual check against the checklist
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The checklist is a plain document usable with any reader

features.title: ATS Discovery Interview Skill
outOfScope: Building the ATS itself
New UI, API endpoints, database tables, or server services
Feature-parity checklist against eRecruit or the market
Quantitative pilot score threshold
features.description: Gives the Manager and Product-Owner personas a guided, research-backed Interview that turns leadership's vision into a Phase 1 MVP brief, a deferred roadmap, and research notes. Gives the Project Admin persona a way to enable it for a pilot project while the existing interview Skill stays as fallback.

outOfScope: Building, buying, or migrating to the replacement ATS itself
New UI, new API endpoints, database tables or migrations, or an ATS-specific server service
Adding ATS logic to the existing general interview Skill
A new interview approach or an external system to store decisions
A feature-parity checklist against eRecruit or the market
A quantitative score threshold for pilot acceptance
Runtime changes to the interview flow, unless the pilot shows the current flow cannot meet a requirement (needs its own PRD)
Changes to Azure DevOps work items
assumptions: Existing project skill settings can register an additional interview Skill option and turn on web research per project
Redaction through Skill instructions reduces risk but cannot guarantee that no identifier reaches a research query
The pilot project is chosen by the Project Admin and Product-Owner before the pilot starts
epics.description: Leadership wants to replace the eRecruit ATS to save money and gain control, but has no agreed Phase 1. This epic delivers one standalone ATS discovery Skill that guides a Manager through a research-backed interview, tracks decisions, protects sensitive details, and produces PRD-ready output. It reuses Apex's existing guided-interview runtime, so it needs no UI, API, or database change.
dependencies: Existing Apex guided-interview runtime: project skill settings, chat persistence and resume, web research access, and interview permissions
successMetrics: The pilot interview passes all six pass conditions: coverage or unresolved labels, correct decision retention, cited influential claims, corroborated material claims, successful resume, and Product-Owner acceptance of the PRD-ready output
The pilot completes with no change to the UI, API, database, or server services
The existing interview Skill still starts normally in the pilot project after the ATS discovery Skill is enabled

personas.name: Manager
personas.description: Leader (stands in for the COO and directors) who runs the ATS discovery Interview and decides what belongs in Phase 1

personas.name: Product-Owner
personas.description: Owner of the ATS replacement outcome who reviews research evidence and accepts the PRD-ready output at the end of the pilot

personas.name: Project Admin
personas.description: Administrator who enables the ATS discovery Skill for the pilot project through project skill settings and keeps the existing interview Skill as fallback

businessRules.rule: Every decision in the ledger has exactly one state: confirmed, assumed, unresolved, or superseded.
When a new answer conflicts with an earlier decision, the interview pauses and asks which decision is authoritative before it moves on.
businessRules.appliesTo: Keep a visible ledger of decisions (PBI)

businessRules.rule: Personal, client, commercial, and internal identifiers are redacted before any web research query is made.
businessRules.appliesTo: Keep sensitive ATS details out of web research (PBI)

businessRules.rule: Research is used only when it informs a decision under discussion, and it tests leadership's decisions rather than driving a feature-parity checklist.
businessRules.appliesTo: Test Phase 1 decisions with cited research (PBI)

businessRules.rule: A claim that influences scope carries a citation with source and date, and a material claim (one that adds, removes, or defers a Phase 1 item) needs corroboration from at least one additional independent source.
businessRules.appliesTo: Test Phase 1 decisions with cited research (PBI)

businessRules.rule: The Skill covers the full staffing lifecycle, but Phase 1 contains only the smallest usable end-to-end workflow. All other scope goes to the deferred roadmap.
businessRules.appliesTo: Shape a Phase 1 MVP through a guided leadership interview (PBI)

businessRules.rule: A session is complete only when every lifecycle area is covered or explicitly labeled unresolved and no conflict is open. Otherwise it remains a draft.
businessRules.appliesTo: Receive a PRD-ready Phase 1 brief, deferred roadmap, and research notes (PBI)

businessRules.rule: Access to ATS discovery Interviews follows existing project scope and the interview view and manage permissions. The Skill adds no new permission, API, table, or UI.
The existing interview Skill remains available in every project as the fallback, and the ATS discovery Skill is released through project skill configuration, pilot project first.
businessRules.appliesTo: Enable the ATS discovery Skill for the pilot project (PBI)

businessRules.rule: The pilot passes only when all pass conditions hold: coverage or unresolved labels, correct decision retention, cited influential claims, corroborated material claims, successful resume, and product owner acceptance of the PRD-ready output. No numeric score is used.
businessRules.appliesTo: Accept or reject the ATS discovery pilot (PBI)

assumptionsMade: The Manager persona stands in for the COO and directors who take part in the leadership interview, because Apex has no separate executive group.
The Product-Owner persona accepts the pilot output, as the transcript names the product owner as the acceptor.

The ADR "ATS System - product interview full scope (research-grounded-ats-discovery-skill)" is accepted, and its decisions are those in the kickoff transcript. Its full text was not available during synthesis.
Existing project skill settings can already register an additional interview Skill option and turn on web research per project, and the chat service passes that research access to the Skill.
Redaction is done by the Skill's instructions to the model. It reduces risk but cannot guarantee that no identifier reaches a research query.
"Benchmark seeds" means a short starting list of ATS products and public sources the Skill uses to begin research, reviewed by the product owner during the pilot.
"Material claim" means a claim that would add, remove, or defer a Phase 1 scope item. "Corroboration" means support from at least one additional independent source.
The "full staffing lifecycle" areas are defined inside the Skill from the ADR and kickoff; the PRD does not list them.
The pilot project is chosen by the Project Admin and product owner before the pilot starts.
Incomplete sessions stay as drafts in the existing in-progress interview state, and the existing mark-complete action is used only after the completion rubric is met.

implementationPhases.rationale: The backlog has one epic, so there is one phase. Inside the feature, the Skill definition (TBI-001) comes first, the ledger and research rules (TBI-002, TBI-003) follow in parallel, then the completion contract (TBI-004), and last the pilot configuration and acceptance checklist (TBI-005, TBI-006) that need the finished Skill.
